independent_probes.name: malformed JSON-RPC boolean response ID
independent_probes.evidence: A direct probe of AppServer.request sent integer request ID 1 and supplied a response with id=true; request() returned its result because True == 1 in Python. The parser also accepts a missing jsonrpc field. This is malformed protocol data that should be rejected.

findings.title: A boolean JSON-RPC response ID matches integer request ID 1
findings.reproduction: The independent direct probe passed {jsonrpc:'2.0', id:true, result:{...}} to request() while its first request ID was 1; request() accepted the result.
findings.impact: Malformed app-server output can satisfy a pending request. The same parser accepts an omitted jsonrpc version. The app-server is a local configured executable, which limits exposure, but malformed responses should fail closed before they can verify catalog/account operations.
findings.recommendation: Require jsonrpc == '2.0' and validate response ID type and exact value before correlating it with a pending integer request ID.

findings.title: max_cost_usd is accepted but never limits provider spend
findings.reproduction: Source inspection confirms _validate_payload only checks that max_cost_usd is a positive finite number; execute_agent discards it as _max_cost. Usage always reports cost_usd:null and uncertain:true. The readiness evidence confirms no independently verified app-server USD measure or provider-enforced ceiling.
findings.impact: Different positive dollar limits have identical execution behavior. This is a material guard gap anywhere max_cost_usd is presented or relied on as a spend ceiling. Time and token limits do not establish a USD billing cap.
findings.recommendation: Treat USD limiting as unsupported and do not describe this adapter as enforcing a dollar budget. A host billing/usage mechanism or revised contract semantics is needed before spend-sensitive acceptance. No spending was authorized for this review.
